goal: Find a representation path that can reproduce an animated GLB in an animated Minecraft Bedrock addon with zero measured loss under the declared validation metric.

vanilla_bedrock.animation_model: Bones define the skeleton; animation files refer to bones by name.

china_polymesh_reference.status: reference format, not yet proven as a vanilla Bedrock runtime format
china_polymesh_reference.direct_glb_mapping_hypothesis: strong structural correspondence, requires runtime/export validation

routes.purpose: test whether poly_mesh attached to animated bones is sufficient
routes.diagnostic: Exact continuous skinning is not representable by the documented vanilla poly_mesh schema when vertices have multiple nonzero influences; this route is retained only as a measured rigid approximation.

quantitative_validation.assignment: triangle with maximum summed source vertex skin weight
quantitative_validation.note: This measures ideal rigid bone deformation against the GLB skin reference before Bedrock runtime serialization. It proves the current rigid projection is not exact for this GLB; it does not measure runtime Euler-animation serialization error.

routes.exporter_status: candidate exporter committed as plugins/haraganzito_bedrock_exporter.js; runtime not validated

routes.purpose: approximate continuous GLB skinning with bone-addressable geometry regions
fallback exploration when native continuous skinning cannot be represented
routes.warning: not equivalent to native continuous skinning unless the runtime representation itself is proven equivalent

routes.purpose: Preserve the complete GLB skin inside Blockbench before Bedrock serialization.

validation.note: Vertex-level native deformation matches the GLB reference within measured floating-point error; scale bind pose and multiplicative scale animation are preserved by the importer.

routes.purpose: Isolate and repair the bind-pose geometry mapping using the supplied working Haraganzito v1.0.0 static poly_mesh as calibration reference.

calibration.scale_diagnostic: The prior rigid candidate applied the GLB skin-container scale to inverse-bind-transformed vertices but omitted the static v1 model-space calibration, producing geometry about 16x too small.
calibration.bind_geometry_method: Compute each bone pivot from inverseBindMatrix^-1 in GLB mesh space, map pivot into calibrated Bedrock space, then store each triangle vertex as world_static_position - bone_pivot with zero bind rotation.

proven: Blockbench issue #2706 documents a separate China polymesh+skeleton+animation format with per-vertex weights
the current documented vanilla poly_mesh schema exposes no per-vertex skin-weight field
Meshy serializes poly_mesh geometry as positions/normals/uvs/polys and does not serialize GLB JOINTS/WEIGHTS/inverse-bind data
Blockbench native ArmatureBone stores per-vertex weights and inverse-bind data, so a loss-preserving intermediate representation exists before Bedrock serialization

Blockbench Armature.calculateVertexDeformation can reproduce the GLB skin deformation formula when the GLB common skin container is kept as an external Group and the native Armature is identity beneath it

A full vertex-level comparison against the Haraganzito GLB gives maximum absolute position error 5.141863423929749e-8 across sampled animation times, consistent with floating-point arithmetic rather than representational loss
not_proven: China reference format loads in normal vanilla Bedrock
vanilla Bedrock poly_mesh directly supports arbitrary per-vertex GLB skin weights
any single conversion route is exact
that native Blockbench weighted skinning can be serialized into a vanilla Bedrock runtime representation without loss
that the native Blockbench weighted Armature representation survives Bedrock geometry export unchanged
conclusion.engineering_decision: Preserve full skinning natively first; treat standard vanilla poly_mesh as a lossy output boundary until a runtime-compatible weighted representation is proven.
